messages.content:
The method WordUtils.abbreviate(String, int, int, String) is meant to abbreviate a string between a lower and upper index with an optional appended string if abbreviation happens.

The key logic for the failure involves these lines:
- At line 618-620, if upper is -1 or larger than str.length(), upper is set to str.length()
- At line 621-624, if upper is less than lower, upper is raised to lower
- At line 627, it looks for the first space after the lower index
- Then at line 629, it calls str.substring(0, upper)

The problem mentioned is that if lower is greater than str.length(), it is not adjusted downward, unlike upper which is capped at str.length(). This leads to upper being set to lower (which is > length) at line 623, then calling str.substring(0, upper) with upper > str.length() which throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

The test case failing is `testAbbreviate()` and the test snippet shows it calls:
`assertEquals("0123456789", WordUtils.abbreviate("0123456789", 15, 20, null));`
Here the string length is 10, but lower is 15 and upper 20. According to the current code:
- upper(20) > str.length(10), so upper = 10 (line 619)
- upper(10) < lower(15), so upper = lower = 15 (line 623)
- Then `str.substring(0, upper)` calls substring(0,15) which throws exception since 15 > 10.

Hence, the bug is that while upper is capped to string length, lower is never capped and can be greater, causing upper to be set above string length and substring to fail.

The current bug report agrees with this:
- "In WordUtils.abbreviate, upper is adjusted to the length of the string, then to lower. But lower is never adjusted to the length of the string, so if lower is greater than str.length(), upper will be too... Then, str.substring(0, upper) throw a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The fix is to adjust lower to the length of the string."

No recent bug reports are relevant here.

# Diagnosis

The problem is caused by the fact that the parameter `lower` is not adjusted/capped to the length of the string. If `lower` is greater than the string length, the subsequent logic sets `upper` to `lower`, which can be out of bounds. This results in the call `str.substring(0, upper)` throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The fix is to add code ensuring `lower` is also capped to str.length(), before adjusting `upper`. This will keep all index values within valid bounds for substring calls.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
